screening_results.reason: No control group or between-group GM volume comparison reported in abstract. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (no comparison of PTSD patients vs controls reported), I2 (no control population described).

Empirical English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter volume between recent-onset PTSD patients (n=10) and trauma-exposed controls without PTSD (n=10). No pharmacological manipulation or lesion study; directly assesses GM differences, meeting I1 and I2.

Empirical English-language MRI voxel-based morphometry study comparing gray matter volume between PTSD patients (fire survivors) and trauma-exposed controls. No pharmacological manipulation, not a lesion study, and not a review. Meets I1 and I2; exclusion criteria not met.

Empirical voxel-based morphometry MRI study comparing gray matter volumes between PTSD patients and trauma-exposed controls, matching inclusion criteria (I1, I2). No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or review) are indicated in the abstract. Full text should be reviewed for details.

Empirical MRI voxel-based morphometry study comparing gray matter volume between combat veterans with PTSD and trauma-exposed controls; no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or review. Meets I1 and I2; exclusion criteria not met.

No comparison between PTSD patients and controls is reported; study assesses trauma-exposed individuals without PTSD only. Exclusion criteria: none met. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (does not evaluate GM volume differences between PTSD patients and controls); I2 not applicable (study sample are subclinical trauma-exposed individuals, not controls in a PTSD vs control comparison).

Abstract examines gray matter volume in OEF/OIF veterans and links deployment/post-deployment experiences to structural brain changes, but does not explicitly state MRI methods nor report comparisons between PTSD patients and controls. No exclusion criteria are evident. Inclusion criteria (I1/I2) cannot be confirmed from abstract alone; full-text needed to determine eligibility.

Empirical English MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray-matter volume between PTSD patients (n=9) and trauma-exposed controls without PTSD (n=16). Meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met; include for full-text review.

Abstract describes an empirical morphometry study measuring regional gray matter volume in trauma survivors, comparing recent-onset PTSD patients to trauma-exposed non-PTSD controls, satisfying I1 and I2. No exclusions (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or review) are indicated in the abstract.

Abstract does not specify that the study used structural MRI morphometry or assessed grey matter volume, nor does it report the control group characteristics. No exclusion criteria are met. Because the abstract provides insufficient detail to confirm I1 and I2, include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Empirical MRI voxel-based morphometry study comparing gray matter volume between cancer survivors with PTSD and two control groups (cancer survivors without PTSD and healthy subjects). No pharmacological manipulations, lesion study, or review. Meets inclusion criteria for GM volume differences in PTSD vs controls.

Empirical English-language structural MRI (3T) voxel-based morphometry study comparing gray matter volume between pediatric PTSD patients (n=27) and healthy non-traumatized controls (n=27). No pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or review. Satisfies I1 and I2; no exclusion criteria met.

Empirical MRI study comparing amygdala (GM) volumes between individuals with history of PTSD and trauma-exposed controls; aligns with review objective of morphometry studies of structural alterations in PTSD. No exclusion criteria (pharmacological/lesion/review) are met in the abstract.

No exclusion criteria met (E1-E3 none). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 — study does not compare PTSD patients with controls; it examines healthy adults and associations between stressful life events and GMV. I2 — not applicable (no PTSD or trauma-exposed control groups). Therefore exclude.

sMRI study comparing gray matter volume and density between 24 pediatric PTSD patients and 24 age- and gender-matched controls, meeting inclusion criteria for MRI assessment of GM differences and appropriate control group. No exclusion criteria (pharmacologic manipulation, lesion study, or review) are met.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I1 — study does not compare PTSD patients with controls; it examines genetic effects in a healthy non-clinical sample. I2 not demonstrated/applicable — although controls are healthy, there is no PTSD-control comparison. Therefore study does not address PTSD-related GM volume differences.

Abstract describes an empirical MRI morphometry study reporting decreased premotor cortex grey matter volume in PTSD patients compared to controls following urban violence, satisfying I1. A control group is implied, satisfying I2. No pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or review is indicated. Include for full-text review to confirm control characteristics and analytic details.

Excluded: Abstract reports structural MRI in previously maltreated but healthy adults and does not include PTSD patient group. Exclusion IDs met: none (E1-E3 not applicable). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (MRI comparison of PTSD patients vs controls) is not met; I2 not applicable because no PTSD group present. No pharmacological, lesion, or review study issues.

Abstract reports structural GMV measures and includes healthy/non-PTSD control groups, but does not clearly report GMV differences between PTSD patients and controls (I1 not demonstrated). Insufficient information to determine I1 from abstract alone; include for full-text review to confirm morphometry group comparisons.

Excluded: study uses diffusion tensor imaging to examine white matter integrity and does not report empirical MRI grey matter (GM) volume comparisons between PTSD patients and controls (I1 not met). Inclusion met: I2 (healthy and trauma-exposed controls included). Exclusion IDs met: none (E1–E3 not applicable).

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (trauma-exposed controls without PTSD). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 — the abstract reports cortical thickness analysis (shape/thickness), not grey matter volume differences; volumetric GM comparisons are not demonstrated. Therefore exclude based on I1 not met.

Empirical English-language MRI study using Voxel-Based Morphometry assessing gray matter density differences between PTSD patients (n=21) and trauma-exposed controls without PTSD (n=22). No pharmacological manipulations, lesion study, or review/meta-analysis reported. Meets inclusion criteria I1 and I2; suitable for full-text review.

Abstract reports an empirical morphometric (gray matter) brain study using monozygotic twin pairs discordant for combat exposure to compare PTSD cases and controls. This satisfies I1 (MRI grey matter volume differences) and I2 (appropriate control population). No exclusion criteria are met.

Meets I1 and I2: empirical English MRI study assessing cortical gray matter volume differences between 25 drug‑naive adult PTSD patients and 25 matched non‑traumatized controls using SIENAX and VBM. No pharmacological manipulations, not a lesion study or review. Include for full-text review.

Abstract investigates volumetric grey matter morphology in the dissociative subtype of PTSD, aligning with the meta-analysis objective on morphometry. However, it does not explicitly state MRI methods or whether PTSD patients were compared to healthy/trauma-exposed controls; full text is needed to confirm inclusion criteria.

Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (study does not assess GM volume differences between PTSD patients and controls; it compares responders vs non-responders within a PTSD sample). I2 not demonstrated (no control population reported).

Empirical English-language MRI study using T1-weighted images and voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter volume between coal mine gas explosion-related PTSD patients (n=14) and non-traumatized controls (n=25). Meets I1 and I2; no exclusion criteria apply. Recommend full-text review for data extraction.

Abstract reports a longitudinal structural MRI study of gray matter development in pediatric PTSD but does not explicitly state comparisons of GM volume between PTSD patients and control groups. No exclusion criteria are met. Insufficient detail to confirm inclusion criterion I1, so include for full-text review to determine if PTSD vs control GM volume comparisons were performed.

Empirical Voxel-based morphometry MRI study including a PTSD group (n=91) and healthy controls, assessing gray matter volume differences; meets I1 and I2. No pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or review—no exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to extract PTSD-specific effect sizes and subgroup details.

Empirical English-language MRI voxel-based morphometry study reporting anterior cingulate gray matter volume differences between PTSD patients and trauma-exposed controls (victims without PTSD); no exclusion criteria met.

Empirical English-language MRI study using Voxel-Based Morphometry comparing grey matter volumes between PTSD patients and both healthy and trauma-exposed controls. No pharmacological manipulations, lesions, or review methods reported. Full-text review appropriate.

Empirical structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) study comparing gray matter volumes between PTSD patients and trauma-exposed controls (combat veterans). Meets I1 (MRI GM volume differences between PTSD and controls) and I2 (controls are trauma-exposed without PTSD). No pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or review is reported. Abstract provides sufficient information for inclusion in full-text review.

The study reports VBM in borderline personality disorder (BPD) patients vs healthy controls and only uses lifetime PTSD as a covariate. It does not assess gray-matter volume differences between PTSD patients and controls, so inclusion criterion I1 is not met. I2 (control type) is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria (E1-E3) are met.

Abstract reports morphovolumetric (structural) changes in 19 drug-naïve PTSD patients compared with 19 healthy controls after EMDR; no exclusions evident (no drugs, lesions, or review). MRI modality/explicit GM-volume statement is not clearly stated in the abstract, so full-text review is required to confirm I1.

Study does not involve PTSD patients or compare PTSD cases vs controls. No exclusion criteria met (E1-E3). Inclusion criteria: I1 not met — not an MRI study comparing PTSD patients and controls; I2 not demonstrated/applicable — although healthy controls are acceptable, there is no PTSD group. Therefore excluded.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (no comparison of PTSD patients to a control group assessing GM volume differences) and I2 (no healthy or trauma-exposed control population demonstrated). The study is a longitudinal within-PTSD patient comparison (responders vs non-responders), so it does not meet the review's requirement for patient vs control morphometry data.

Empirical MRI voxel-based morphometry study comparing hippocampal and anterior cingulate grey matter volumes between PTSD patients and trauma-exposed controls; no exclusion criteria met and it addresses structural GM alterations in PTSD.

Abstract reports associations between brain volumes and PTSD symptoms but does not specify that it assessed GM volume differences between PTSD patients and control groups. Exclusion criteria not met; inclusion criterion I1 (GM volume differences vs controls) is not demonstrated from abstract alone. Insufficient information to determine inclusion, so include for full-text review.

Abstract reports rACC volume predicting CBT treatment response in PTSD but does not state comparisons between PTSD patients and control groups or explicit GM volume difference analyses. No exclusion criteria are met. Inclusion criterion I1 (GM volume differences between PTSD and controls) is not demonstrated in the abstract; insufficient information to determine, so include for full-text review.

Abstract reports investigation of PTSD-related structural alterations consistent with morphometry objectives, but does not explicitly state MRI, gray matter volume measures, or details of control group. No exclusion criteria are met. Insufficient methodological detail for definitive inclusion, so include for full-text review to confirm MRI-based GM comparisons.

Abstract reports an empirical volumetric investigation of grey matter reductions in PTSD (contrasted with major depression) relevant to morphometry meta-analysis. It does not specify the control group details or explicitly state MRI modality, so full-text review is needed to confirm control type and methods.

Empirical VBM MRI study (English) comparing GMV in 30 PTSD patients and 30 healthy controls; meets I1 (MRI study assessing GMV differences between PTSD and controls) and I2 (controls are healthy individuals). No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or review) are met, so include for full-text review.

Abstract reports MRI and SPECT neuroimaging comparing PTSD patients and controls but does not specify assessment of grey matter volume or the type of control group. No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, review) are evident. Insufficient abstract detail to confirm I1 or I2, so include for full-text review.

Title indicates a voxel-based morphometry study of grey matter in rape victims with PTSD, matching the meta-analysis topic. However the abstract text is not provided here and it is unclear whether MRI GM volume comparisons with an appropriate control group are reported. No exclusion criteria are evident. Insufficient information to confirm all inclusion criteria, so include for full-text review.

No control group reported; study reports correlations of childhood maltreatment with prefrontal gray matter volumes within PTSD patients only. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (no GM volume comparison between PTSD and controls), I2 (no control population reported).

Excluded: No PTSD patient group or PTSD vs control GM volume comparison. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (study does not assess GM volume differences between PTSD patients and controls); I2 not demonstrated (sample consists of trauma-exposed individuals without PTSD rather than a PTSD group compared to controls).

Voxel-based morphometry MRI study examining grey matter volume in adults with and without PTSD (PTSD diagnosis included as a predictor), comparing trauma-exposed bereaved parents; meets inclusion of empirical GM volume MRI and uses trauma-exposed controls. No exclusion criteria are met. Abstract provides sufficient basis for full-text review to confirm group comparisons and extract data.

No exclusion criteria met (E1-E3 none). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 — study does not assess grey matter volume differences between PTSD patients and controls; it examines post-traumatic growth and within-subject rGMV changes after a disaster. I2 not demonstrated.

Empirical MRI study reporting grey matter volumetric differences between youth with PTSD and both trauma-exposed (without PTSD) and healthy controls; meets I1 (GM volume MRI study) and I2 (appropriate control groups). No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or review) are met.
